claims.assertion: Swaruu says one numeric destination code includes all navigation and timing data.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)

claims.assertion: Warp matches a ship’s toroidal frequency to a destination, taking it through the ether for instantaneous travel.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)

claims.assertion: Portals use the same frequency principle, but return usually requires a separate portal physically at the destination.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)

claims.assertion: Portal frequencies can use magnet relations or counter-rotating red-mercury rings; ship turbines and computers control an analogous field.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)

claims.assertion: She says incomplete destination data can merge arrivals with surrounding objects, citing the Philadelphia Experiment.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)
